data: Tesla's net income attributable to common stockholders was about $12.56 billion in fiscal 2022 (GAAP, roughly $12.6 billion, with total net income including noncontrolling interests near $12.58 billion) and about $7.09 billion in fiscal 2024 (roughly $7.1 billion attributable to common stockholders). That works out to a decline of approximately 43.5% over the two years, driven mainly by lower average selling prices, higher operating expenses and reduced automotive margins, partly offset by growth in energy storage and interest income. Note that the fiscal 2024 figure benefited from a one-time effect in 2023 that did not recur, as 2023 had included a roughly $5.9 billion tax valuation allowance release, so the 2023 comparison would look quite different. Figures are from Tesla's annual 10-K filings and I am citing them from memory rather than from a live lookup, so please verify against the filings before relying on them.
